signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.72, holding above its SMA20 of 156.40 but pinned below the SMA50/200 resistance band at 158.45/158.60. CFTC positioning shows JPY Leveraged Funds net long +4,472 contracts, sitting at the 98th percentile of its trailing 52-week distribution (z=+2.66). While the nominal policy spread of 275bp (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) supports the underlying carry structure, options positioning signals extreme hedging demand. The 25-delta Risk Reversal prints at -2.28, reflecting a pronounced put skew in USD/JPY. Concurrently, 1M ATM implied volatility of 8.7% trades below 30-day realized volatility of 10.0%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of -1.4%. Bond market stress diverges from equities, with MOVE at its 96th percentile trailing rank while VIX sits at its 8th percentile. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; aggressive options downside hedging limits spot topside despite the carry buffer. Catalyst: Japan Retail Sales and Industrial Production prints at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot clears the SMA50/200 band at 158.60, forcing a cover of downside put structures.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Support + RBA Decision
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7026, resting directly on its 200-day moving average at 0.7026 while remaining below the descending SMA20 and SMA50 at 0.7141 and 0.7096. Leveraged funds hold a sizable net long of +55,684 contracts, though weekly positioning declined by -3,615 contracts. The RBA cash rate sits at 4.35% versus the Fed policy rate at 4.00%, maintaining a 35bp Australian cash rate carry premium, supported by a negative OIS differential of -47bp in AUD's favor. Spot price action tests major structural support ahead of the domestic central bank event. A failure of the 200-day moving average exposes speculative longs to rapid liquidation. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; technical defense of the 200-day baseline aligned with positive carry differential. Catalyst: RBA Interest Rate Decision and Statement at 04:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close below the 200-day moving average at 0.7026 triggers an unwind of crowded spec longs.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 4.00% — -35bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers a 1.090% performance spread across G10 crosses over the rolling week. JPY leads the G10 complex with an average return of +0.602% across 7 pairs, while CHF lags the peer group at -0.488% across 6 pairs. CHF/JPY trades at 189.99, having crossed above the SNB 0.00% versus BoJ 1.25% carry gap of +125bp favoring the yen. Speculative positioning corroborates the divergence: Leveraged Funds are heavily net short CHF at -18,620 contracts (2nd percentile, z=-2.30), whereas JPY net positioning sits in the 98th percentile. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; bilateral divergence driven by BoJ tightening expectations against an accommodative zero-rate SNB. Catalyst: Switzerland KOF Economic Barometer at 07:00 UTC. Risk: Reversal of JPY outperformance with CHF/JPY breaking higher toward fair value model resistance at 196.44.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Bearish Moving Average Structure + Real Yield Drift
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1390, pinned beneath its descending moving average stack with SMA20 at 1.1539, SMA50 at 1.1538, and SMA200 at 1.1625. Central bank rates maintain a 135bp nominal differential favoring the dollar, with the Fed policy rate at 4.00% versus the ECB deposit facility at 2.65%. US 5-year yields rose +25bp over the trailing 5 sessions (FRED, as of Sep 24), decomposed into real yields +24bp and breakeven inflation +1bp, highlighting a real-yield-led rate drive. Leveraged funds hold a net short EUR position of -58,805 contracts, expanding downside exposure by -7,450 contracts week-over-week. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent real yield support for the dollar reinforcing negative technical momentum. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 11:00 UTC. Risk: A sustained breakout above the SMA20/50 resistance cluster at 1.1540 invalidates the short setup.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% — 135bp USD carry advantage
